Part I — Knowledge Base (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Knowledge Base (Session 94, English)
Aura-Checking Roll Call and the Teaching on Ahuti Shakti: Why Repetition of One Mantra Creates Miracles

This session is a live Mool T atva aura-checking r oll call (continuing a check-in pr ocess fr om the pr evious day , interrupted by a network issue), interspersed thr oughout with an extended teaching on mantra shakti, ahuti (fir e-offering) shakti, and the discipline of single-mantra devotion. Privacy note: per Ashaeiynn's standing policy against publicly detailing individuals' specific negativity/pitru/tantra diagnoses, the r oll-call findings in this document ar e summarized into general categories/patterns rather than r epr oduced as name-by-name diagnoses; testimonies of positive change ar e included only wher e they wer e general and voluntary , without pairing a name to a specific spiritual diagnosis. This session includes extensive live back-and-forth, so it is pr esented as a full 3-part document.

1. Opening Invocation: The Sankalp Prayer Recited Befor e Roll-Call Checking The session opens with the speaker leading the group in a formal sankalp (resolve) prayer before beginning jaap: devotees are asked to bow to Dharti Mata (Mother Earth), wash their hands and feet, and recite together , invoking Hanuman ji Maharaj with Ashaeiynn's Parikshit Bhaiya as witness, of fering their jaap and asking for protection and inclusion in the collective raksha-suraksha (protection) sankalp.

2. Format: A Live Mool Tatva Aura-Checking Roll Call, Continued Fr om the Pr evious Day The speaker explains that this session continues a roll-call aura-checking process that was interrupted the previous day by a network issue, checking devotees one by one by name to confirm whether they have experienced positive change ("fark") since beginning their practice, followed by a brief spiritual reading for each.

3. Aggr egate Pattern (Privacy Note): General Categories of Findings Across This Roll-Call Session Rather than detailing each individual's specific reading, this document summarizes the pattern observed across the session: the lar ge majority of devotees checked showed no negativity and reported positive changes since beginning jaap; a smaller number showed light residual pitru (ancestral spirit) influence, described as fading gradually with continued practice; a few showed a combination of negativity and tantra (black-magic) influence requiring more sustained practice and, in some cases, an in-person visit; and a small number were noted as carrying an existing spiritual siddhi (attainment) or connection to a shaktipeeth (power site) from before joining Ashaeiynn.

4. Mahotsav Dates and Attendance Windows Announced The speaker announces that this year's Mahotsav begins on the 25th, with a peak period from the 28th through the 5th–8th, and that the 1st through 10th are also considered a good time to attend; Maha Dashami, described as an especially significant day , falls on September 2nd, and attending around that date is said to bring exceptional benefit.

5. Teaching: Distance/Remote Jaap Works Just as Well as In-Person Practice The speaker reassures devotees that remote participation is fully ef fective — using the metaphor that just as a video streams acceptably at 1080p without needing "ultra-pro HD," a devotee's practice from home carries genuine spiritual benefit without requiring in-person presence.

6. Teaching: Any Unr esolved Pr oblem Can Be Addressed by Attending Mahotsav In Person The speaker states that devotees who feel a lingering issue or dosh (spiritual af fliction) that hasn't been resolved remotely are encouraged to attend Mahotsav in person,
where some saint present is promised to of fer them grace and guidance.

7. Teaching: "Aaram" (Comfort) Comes Fr om Choosing "Raam" — A Wordplay Teaching on Priorities The speaker of fers a wordplay teaching: those who love comfort ("aaram") chose comfort, and those who love work chose work — but the speaker teaches that the surest path to genuine comfort is to instead choose "Raam" (Ram), playing on the near -identical sound of the two words.

8. Teaching: Time for Jaap Is a Matter of Priority , Not Availability The speaker challenges the common complaint that there's no time for an hour of daily jaap, pointing out that even people in extremely demanding roles (citing directors and vice-chancellor -level professionals working eight-plus-hour days abroad) manage six hours of daily jaap — concluding that availability of time is entirely a matter of priority .

9. Teaching: Jaap Reduces the Need for Sleep, Rather Than Incr easing It The speaker teaches that beginning consistent jaap practice tends to reduce a person's need for sleep over time — framing excessive sleep itself as something that can leave a person feeling more fatigued than adequate jaap practice would.

10. Teaching: Devotion Requir es Setting Aside Time Specifically for One's Ishta (Personal Deity) The speaker teaches that a person should set aside dedicated time for their own spiritual practice and personal deity (ishta), not only for family and work obligations, framing this as a necessary and non-selfish use of time.

1 1. Teaching: Meeting Fellow Devotees and Saints Reawakens One's "Purva Tattva" (Past-Life Spiritual Element) The speaker teaches that gathering in person with fellow devotees and saints reawakens a devotee's dormant "purva tattva" (an element or aptitude carried over from past lives), producing conversations and insight not otherwise accessible even among one's own family — illustrated with the saying "strong people make strong places," not the reverse.

12. Illustration: A Government Officer Who Found Time for Mahotsav Once He Made It a Priority The speaker recounts a devotee, a government of ficer who initially said he couldn't get leave, who suddenly managed to arrange leave and book a flight once Mahotsav became his true priority — used to illustrate that people generally can find time for what genuinely matters to them.

13. Q&A: Why Hasn't My Divine Vision (Drishti) Opened After Years of Practice? A devotee shares that despite significant time spent on mantra jaap, they haven't experienced much visible change and asks why . The speaker responds by first noting the specific spiritual reading given the previous day (summarized in Section 3 above, per this document's privacy approach) and invites the devotee to attend Mahotsav for further personalized guidance.

14. Teaching: Mantra Shakti Is Gr eater Than Drishti (Divine Vision) Responding to a related question from another devotee (ten hours of daily jaap for three months without an opened drishti), the speaker teaches that mantra shakti (mantra power) is a far greater attainment than drishti, which he describes as a comparatively small thing; drishti can appear the moment a saint chooses to grant it, but sustained mantra practice builds power that outlasts and outweighs the ability to simply "see."

15. Teaching: The Staged Levels of Mantra Shakti by Jaap Count The speaker lays out a specific framework (as taught in this session) describing spiritual capability unlocked at escalating cumulative jaap counts: at roughly 50 lakh to 1 crore repetitions, the mantra begins to "awaken" and vibrate; from 1 to 1.5 crore, the practitioner can begin to use the mantra to help others; from 3 to 4 crore, the mantra can "cut" (remove) many obstacles; above 6 crore, it can remove others' doshas; from 7 to 8 crore, a practitioner can remove their own doshas as well as others'; near 14 crore, the deity is described as manifesting directly; and at 22 crore, one's own will/intention is said to directly shape outcomes.

16. Teaching: Even Pr olonged Jaap Without Visible Results Is Itself a Sign of Grace The speaker reassures a devotee doing ten hours of daily jaap without an opened drishti that sustained practice at that level is itself proof of divine grace (since such sustained sitting requires a saint's blessing to be possible at all), and playfully suggests that an unopened drishti may even be protecting her from stopping her practice too soon.

17. Teaching: Guru Nanak's Disciplined Jaap Schedule as a Historical Example of Mantra Siddhi The speaker cites Guru Nanak's reported daily discipline — sleeping around 9 p.m., waking at 1 a.m., bathing and preparing, then sitting in jaap by a riverside from

roughly 1:45 a.m. until 9 a.m. before attending to daily duties — as a historical illustration of how sustained, disciplined mantra practice produced immense spiritual power , including the ability to counter tantric attacks and heal illness through mantra alone.

18. Teaching: A Mantra Requir es Guru Diksha (Initiation) to Become Siddha (Empower ed) The speaker teaches that for a mantra to become fully siddha (empowered), it generally requires proper guru diksha (initiation); a self-started or informally acquired mantra can still work, but typically requires two to three crore repetitions before its power becomes reliably active, with darshan (visionary experience) commonly reported above six crore repetitions.

19. Q&A: Should a Devotee Also Continue a Separate Family or Personal Deity's Mantra? A devotee asks whether they should continue practicing an earlier personal or family deity's mantra alongside Jai Siyaram. The speaker responds that once a devotee has received the Jai Siyaram mantra and its associated guru lineage, they are guided to focus exclusively on that mantra going forward, rather than continuing to split practice between multiple mantras.

20. Teaching: Why Ashaeiynn Moved Fr om Multiple Deity Offerings to a Single Mantra Two Years Ago The speaker shares that in Ashaeiynn's earlier havan practice (roughly four years ago), ahuti (fire of ferings) were made to a wide range of deities in sequence (Ganesh, village deities, kul devta, and others), until the speaker's guru taught, about two years ago, that this practice should be simplified to a single, repeated mantra and of fering.

21. Teaching: The Loophole Risk of Offering Ahuti to Multiple Differ ent Deities The speaker explains the reasoning behind that change: each distinct mantra/deity of fering opens its own separate spiritual "loophole" tied to that specific mantra's ener gy , through which negativity or an attack could theoretically enter — so of fering to many dif ferent deities in sequence multiplies the number of such vulnerabilities.

22. Teaching: The Concept of "Ahuti Shakti" — Why Repeating One Mantra Builds Unmatched Cumulative Power The speaker teaches that consistently repeating jaap and havan of ferings to a single mantra, over years, builds a specific kind of cumulative power called "ahuti shakti" (of fering power) that eventually becomes so concentrated that no equivalent or opposing ener gy can be generated to match it — a power unavailable to those who scatter their of ferings across many dif ferent mantras.

23. Teaching: "Repetition Cr eates Miracles" — The Principle Behind Single-Mantra Devotion The speaker summarizes the underlying principle in English as "repetition creates miracles," teaching that awakening (jagrit-karan) and the emer gence of real spiritual power come specifically from sustained repetition of one practice, not from variety .

24. Teaching: Never Abandon Your Guru Mantra, Even If Tested The speaker teaches that a devotee should never abandon their guru mantra under any circumstance — going so far as to say that even if the guru himself were to appear and instruct a devotee to stop chanting Jai Siyaram, the correct devotional response would still be unwavering continuation, since true devotion is tested precisely at such moments.

25. Story: Param Anand ji Maharaj and the Refusal of Impersonal Enlightenment The speaker recounts the story of a saint, Param Anand ji Maharaj, who experienced deep, sustained devotional bliss (multiple-hour visitations from the divine mother) during his practice; when later of fered a path to formal "enlightenment" (symbolically described as detaching entirely from that devotional connection), he declined — reasoning that the devotional joy he already experienced was worth more than an abstract attainment that would end that intimate relationship, and that such formal enlightenment might make him a "great saint" in name only , without preserving what he valued most.

26. Teaching: "Mata Ram, Mat Pita Ramachandra" — Reinterpr eting a Hanuman Chalisa Line as a Teaching About the Mantra Itself The speaker reinterprets a well-known devotional line ("Mata Ram, Mat Pita Ramachandra, Swami Ram, Mat Sakha Ramachandra" — "Ram is my mother , Ram is my father , Ram is my master , Ram is my friend") as Hanuman ji referring not literally to Lord Ram as a person in every role, but to the Ram mantra itself functioning as mother , father , master, and friend — extending this teaching to Ashaeiynn's own Jai Siyaram mantra as fulfilling that same complete role for its practitioners, since a personal deity or shrine may not always be physically accessible, but the mantra itself always is.

27. Teaching: The Mantra Even Binds the Divine The speaker cites the line "Sumire pawan sut paavan naama, apne hi vas kari rakhe Rama" ("remembering the pure name of the son of the wind [Hanuman], he keeps Ram bound to his own will") to teach that consistent devotion to a single mantra is powerful enough, in this tradition's framing, to bind divine presence closely to the practitioner .

28. Story: Vibhishan's Imperfect Life and Unwavering Faith in Hanuman ji's Mantra The speaker recounts that Vibhishan — a devotee from a rakshasa (demon) lineage who, even by the tradition's own account, ate meat and had multiple wives after becoming king of Lanka — nonetheless attained lasting spiritual immortality and is still honored today , explained entirely by his sustained faith in Hanuman ji's mantra ("T umharo mantra Vibhishan maana, Lankeshwar bhaye sab jag jaana"), used here to teach that unwavering faith in one's mantra, not external behavioral perfection, is what carries lasting spiritual power .

29. Teaching: Hanuman ji Never Prescribed Dietary or Behavioral Restrictions Continuing from the Vibhishan story , the speaker teaches that Hanuman ji himself never instructed devotees to maintain celibacy , avoid onion and garlic, avoid non-vegetarian food, or exclude women from worshipping him — stating plainly that these are restrictions later traditions and people added themselves, not teachings that appear in Hanuman ji's own recorded character (citing works like the Vinaya Patrika as showing no such restrictions).

30. Illustration: Krishna and Arjuna Still Chanting "Jai Shr ee Ram" in Battle The speaker of fers a devotional, imaginative illustration in which Hanuman ji continues chanting "Jai Shree Ram" even during the Mahabharata war and in the presence of Krishna and Arjuna, who join in — used to playfully illustrate that a devotee should never set aside their chosen mantra regardless of circumstance, since even Krishna is depicted here as honoring rather than replacing it.

31. Closing Teaching: "Jaisa Guru Chahte Hain, Waisa Ho Raha Hai" (What the Guru Wills, Happens) The session closes with the speaker reflecting that Mahotsav preparations are not proceeding as he personally envisioned, but exactly as his guru wills — of fering this as a final teaching on surrender , before confirming the group will reconvene the next day at the same time.
QUICK RULES SUMMARY

This session is a live Mool Tatva aura-checking roll call combined with an extended teaching on mantra and ahuti (fireof fering) shakti; it is a full 3-part document given extensive live interaction throughout. Per Ashaeiynn's privacy policy , individual roll-call findings are summarized here into general categories rather than reproduced name-by-name; specific negativity/pitru/tantra diagnoses tied to named individuals are not detailed in this document. Mahotsav this year runs from the 25th, with peak benefit around the 28th through the 5th–8th and Maha Dashami on September 2nd; remote/distance jaap is taught to be fully ef fective, comparable to "1080p" video quality . Mantra shakti (accumulated through sustained repetition) is taught to be a greater attainment than drishti (divine vision); this session lays out staged jaap-count milestones (roughly 50 lakh through 22 crore) at which dif ferent spiritual capabilities are said to emer ge. A mantra requires guru diksha (initiation) to become fully siddha (empowered); once initiated into the Jai Siyaram mantra and lineage, a devotee is guided to practice that single mantra exclusively rather than splitting focus across multiple deities. Central teaching: repeated devotion to a single mantra builds concentrated "ahuti shakti" unmatched by scattering of ferings across multiple deities — summarized as "repetition creates miracles." A devotee should never abandon their guru mantra, even when tested. Hanuman ji himself is taught to have never prescribed dietary or behavioral restrictions (celibacy , food rules, gender exclusions) — these are described as later additions, not his own teaching; Vibhishan's story is cited as an example of imperfect conduct paired with unwavering mantra faith still yielding lasting spiritual attainment. Spelling note: the institute's name is written "Ashaeiynn" — use this spelling consistently .
Part II — Q&A Pairs (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Q&A Pairs (Session 94, English)
Aura-Checking Roll Call and the Teaching on Ahuti Shakti: Why Repetition of One Mantra Creates Miracles
User-style questions with answers gr ounded in this session's aura-checking r oll call and its extended teaching on mantra and ahuti shakti.

Q1. What prayer is recited befor e jaap in this tradition? A: Per this teaching, devotees bow to Dharti Mata, wash their hands and feet, and recite a sankalp prayer invoking Hanuman ji Maharaj with Ashaeiynn's Parikshit Bhaiya as witness, of fering their jaap and asking to be included in the collective protection sankalp.

Q2. When is Mahotsav happening this year , and when is the best time to attend? A: Per this teaching, Mahotsav begins on the 25th, with a peak period from the 28th through the 5th–8th (the 1st through 10th also being a good window); Maha Dashami on September 2nd is described as an especially significant day to attend.

Q3. Does r emote/distance jaap work as well as attending in person? A: Yes — per this teaching, remote practice is described as fully ef fective, compared to how a video still looks good at "1080p" without needing "ultra-pro HD."

Q4. Why does this teaching say people don't have time for an hour of daily jaap? A: Per this teaching, lack of time is described as purely a matter of priority , not true unavailability — illustrated by professionals in extremely demanding roles who still manage several hours of daily jaap.
Q5. Does mor e jaap mean needing mor e sleep? A: No — per this teaching, consistent jaap practice tends to reduce a person's need for sleep over time, rather than increase it.

Q6. Why does this teaching encourage attending in-person gatherings with fellow devotees? A: Per this teaching, gathering with fellow devotees and saints reawakens a devotee's dormant "purva tattva" (past-life spiritual element), producing insight and connection not accessible even within one's own family .

Q7. If my mantra jaap hasn't pr oduced visible r esults (like an opened drishti) after a long time, what does this teaching say? A: Per this teaching, mantra shakti (accumulated mantra power) is a far greater attainment than drishti (divine vision) — drishti can open the moment a saint chooses to grant it, but sustained practice builds power that outlasts and outweighs simply being able to "see."

Q8. What jaap-count milestones does this teaching associate with differ ent spiritual capabilities? A: Per this teaching's framework: roughly 50 lakh–1 crore repetitions begins to awaken the mantra; 1–1.5 crore allows using the mantra to help others; 3–4 crore allows "cutting" obstacles; above 6 crore allows removing others' doshas; 7–8 crore allows removing one's own doshas as well; near 14 crore, the deity is said to manifest directly; and at 22 crore, one's will is said to directly shape outcomes.

Q9. What historical example does this teaching cite for disciplined mantra practice? A: Per this teaching, Guru Nanak's reported schedule (sleeping around 9 p.m., waking at 1 a.m., and sitting in riverside jaap from about 1:45 a.m. to 9 a.m.) is cited as an example of how sustained discipline produced immense spiritual power .

Q10. Does a mantra need formal initiation (guru diksha) to become powerful? A: Per this teaching, a mantra generally requires guru diksha to become fully siddha (empowered); a self-started or informally learned mantra can still work but typically needs two to three crore repetitions before its power reliably activates, with darshan commonly reported above six crore.

Q1 1. Should a devotee keep practicing an earlier family deity's mantra alongside Jai Siyaram? A: No — per this teaching, once initiated into the Jai Siyaram mantra and its guru lineage, a devotee is guided to focus exclusively on that mantra rather than splitting practice across multiple mantras.

Q12. Why did Ashaeiynn move to using a single mantra in havan rather than offering to many deities? A: Per this teaching, roughly four years ago havan of ferings were made to a sequence of dif ferent deities, until the speaker's guru taught (about two years ago) that this should be simplified to one repeated mantra, since each separate mantra/deity of fering opens its own spiritual "loophole" that could be exploited by negativity or attack.

Q13. What is "ahuti shakti"? A: Per this teaching, ahuti shakti is the concentrated cumulative power built by repeating jaap and fireof ferings to a single mantra over years — a power the teaching says becomes so strong that no equivalent opposing ener gy can be generated to match it, unavailable to those who scatter of ferings across many dif ferent mantras.

Q14. What is the cor e principle behind this teaching's appr oach to mantra practice? A: Per this teaching, the principle is summarized as "repetition creates miracles" — spiritual awakening and real power come specifically from sustained repetition of one practice, not variety .

Q15. Should a devotee ever abandon their guru mantra? A: No — per this teaching, a devotee should never abandon their guru mantra under any circumstance, even in a hypothetical scenario where the guru himself instructed them to stop, since true devotion is tested precisely at such moments.

Q16. What is the story of Param Anand ji Maharaj, and what does it teach? A: Per this teaching, Param Anand ji Maharaj experienced deep devotional bliss through his practice, and when later of fered a path to formal, impersonal "enlightenment," he declined — teaching that the joy of an ongoing devotional relationship can be valued above an abstract spiritual attainment that would end it.

Q17. What does the line "Mata Ram, Mat Pita Ramachandra" mean in this teaching's interpr etation? A: Per this teaching, this line is reinterpreted as Hanuman ji describing the Ram mantra itself — not a literal deity always physically present — as functioning as mother , father , master, and friend; Ashaeiynn's Jai Siyaram mantra is taught to serve this same complete role for its practitioners.

Q18. What does the phrase "Sumir e pawan sut paavan naama, apne hi vas kari rakhe Rama" mean? A: Per this teaching, it means that by remembering Hanuman ji's pure name, devotion becomes powerful enough to keep divine presence bound close to the practitioner — used to illustrate the mantra's binding power .

Q19. What is the story of Vibhishan, and what does it teach about devotion? A: Per this teaching, Vibhishan — a rakshasa-lineage devotee who, by the tradition's own account, ate meat and had multiple wives after becoming king of Lanka — nonetheless attained lasting spiritual immortality , entirely attributed to his unwavering faith in Hanuman ji's mantra; the lesson taught is that steadfast faith, not external behavioral perfection, carries lasting spiritual power .

Q20. Did Hanuman ji himself pr escribe restrictions like celibacy , avoiding onion/garlic, or excluding women fr om his worship? A: No — per this teaching, the speaker states plainly that Hanuman ji never prescribed such restrictions; these were added later by tradition and people, not by Hanuman ji's own recorded teaching or character .

Q21. What closing r eflection did the speaker offer about Mahotsav pr eparations? A: Per this teaching's closing, the speaker reflects that preparations are not unfolding as he personally envisioned, but exactly as his guru wills — of fered as a teaching on surrender , before confirming the group would reconvene the next day .
Bot Response Guidelines

Do not reproduce or speculate about any specific individual's negativity/pitru/tantra diagnosis from this session's roll call; refer only to the general categories described in the Knowledge Base's privacy-summarized Section 3. When explaining why Ashaeiynn practices a single mantra, ground the answer in this session's specific "ahuti shakti" and "loophole" framing rather than generic mantra theory . Part III — Curated Conversational Q&A (Hinglish)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Curated Conversational Q&A (Session 94, Hinglish)
Aura-Checking Roll Call and the Teaching on Ahuti Shakti: Why Repetition of One Mantra Creates Miracles

This is NOT an exhaustive transcript of every exchange in this session. Only conversations judged genuinely valuable and likely to benefit futur e users ar e included, each with a short italicized note explaining why it was kept. Per Ashaeiynn's privacy policy , individual negativity/pitru/tantra diagnoses ar e not r epr oduced her e even wher e they appear in the sour ce transcript.
Exchange 1 — "Why Hasn't Much Changed Despite Long Jaap?"

Vivek: Ek cheez jaanna chah raha tha main ki abhi kaafi samay ho gaya mere ko mantra jaap karte hue, lekin fir bhi bahut zyada kuch cheezein change nahi ho rahi. Toh kahan dikkat aa rahi hai? Bhaiya: Kahan dikkat aa rahi hai bhai? Humne kal bhi yahi likhwaya tha, tumhe pata hai. Vivek bhai, ek kaam karo — aap Mahotsav mein aa jao, toh hum dekh ke iss samasya ko aage tumhare liye uchit margdarshan de denge. Vivek: Ji Bhaiya, dhanyawad Bhaiya.

Why this is her e: A genuinely common question — long practice without visible change — answer ed with a clear , actionable next step (attend in person for personalized guidance) rather than a diagnosis. The specific r eading given is intentionally left out her e per this tradition's privacy appr oach to negativity/pitru findings.
Exchange 2 — Ten Hours of Jaap, No Drishti Yet

Rakhi: Bhaiya main toh 10 ghante kar rahi hoon, teen mahine ho gaye, abhi tak nahi khuli. Bhaiya: Tum kaun bol rahi ho? Rakhi: Rakhi. Bhaiya: Achha, tumhe darshan hote hain Rakhi? Aise mat bolo. Theek hai bhaiya, mujhe mehsoos nahi ho raha na, main kya karoon batao. Rakhi: Bhaiya mera jab bhi 10 ghante ho jaata hai aaram se, aur maine toh pichhle do-teen hafte se aur bhi zyada... dedh lakh ke aaspaas kar rahi hoon jap. Bhaiya: Toh wahi main keh raha hoon na — drishti se bada mantra shakti hoti hai. Mantra shakti jitni badi hoti hai, drishti bahut chhoti cheez hai mantra shakti ke aage. Abhi kya hai, aap drishti ke chakkar mein mantra jaap kar rahe ho — kal jab aapka mantra jaap itna bada ho jayega tab aap aisi lakhon drishtiyan daan kar sakte ho.

Why this is her e: A dir ect, sincer e question many long-practicing devotees ar e likely to ask, met with a clear r eframing of priorities (mantra shakti over drishti) — genuinely new teaching content deliver ed thr ough dialogue that isn't captur ed elsewher e in this session's monologue sections.
Exchange 3 — The Cror e-Count Question

Mayank: Bhaiya maine aapki video dekhi. Aapne usme pehle bola 50 lakh se ek crore hona chahiye. Phir uske baad bola ek se dedh crore hona chahiye. Phir uske baad bola dedh se do crore hona chahiye. Aur mera tar get uss hisaab se badhta ja raha hai. Bhaiya:

Behen main aapko bata deta hoon — jis din 14 crore ho jayega, uss se pehle aapko khuli aankhon se bhagwan darshan denge, sakshaat darshan denge aur vardaan hoga aapke paas. Main aapko waise nahi keh raha — ek se dedh crore ka matlab aapka mantra jagrit ho jayega. 50 se 1 lakh mein aapka mantra mein vibration aane lagti hai, tarang se judne lagta hai. Aap jab dedh crore se 2 crore mein pahunch jaate ho toh aapke mantra mein badi shakti aa jaati hai — uss mantra se aap kisi ka upyog kar sakte hain. Teen se 4 crore jab ho jaata hai toh mantra jaap se aap bahut cheezon ko kaat sakte hain. Jab 6 crore se upar jaata hai toh aap logon ke doshon ko bhi khatam kar sakte hain...

Why this is her e: A rar e instance of the speaker laying out the full staged mantra-shakti framework in dir ect response to a devotee's genuine confusion about shifting numbers — valuable because it clarifies that the milestones ar e cumulative stages, not a single moving tar get.
Exchange 4 — "Anshu Bhai ya Anshu Behen?"

Devotee 1: Ye Anshu Didi jaisi lag rahi thi, ye Anshu Didi ki awaaz thi. Devotee 2: Anshu Bhai — Anshu Behen nahi ho sakte Bhaiya. Devotee 1: Ab main online hoon na toh aap toh kar sakte ho — ye aapne Anshu Bhai karke sabko apni side kar liya. Devotee 3: Ye Anshu Bhai hai ya Anshu Behen hai? Humne aaj tak darshan bhi nahi kiye. Main naya hoon, mujhe pata hi nahi hai. Bhaiya: Apne mukh se jis roop mein maano leti hai, waisi ho jaati hai — main kehti hoon Anshu Behen hai. Mere pati kehte hain Anshu Bhai hai. Jis roop mein maano wahi roop le leti hai. (a devotee quotes): Jaaki rahi bhavana jaisi, prabhu moorat dekhi tin taisi. Bhaiya: Dekho, Anshu hamari gudiya hai, hamari behen hai — kabhi hamara bhai ban jaati hai, kabhi behen, kabhi badi behen, kabhi choti behen. Masti karti rehti hai, chulbuli si hai — behen-bhai ka prem.

Why this is her e: A warm, funny moment of genuine sangat back-and-forth that lands on a r eal teaching point (the T ulsidas line about per ception shaping how the divine appears to each devotee) — light-hearted but with r eal devotional content, exactly the kind of "valuable and new" exchange this curated section is meant to captur e.
Note on Curation

The individual roll-call exchanges involving specific negativity , pitru, or tantra readings tied to named devotees were deliberately left out of this curated section (and are only summarized in aggregate, anonymized form in Part I), consistent with Ashaeiynn's stated policy against publicly detailing individuals' spiritual diagnoses.
